review_scope: Environment-only offline recovery; frozen campaign and research remain unchanged. No installer was executed by this reviewer.

candidate.note: Concurrent author may have changed the candidate after this snapshot; verdict does not transfer to other bytes.

findings.location: STAGE_PATH assignment, lines 77, 273-306; fixed receipt writes at 286-289
findings.issue: The new recovery still writes resumable-torch-stage-status.json and re-writes several previous cancellation/failure receipt files.
findings.evidence: It copies prior status to a timestamped file then calls write_json(STAGE_PATH, status). The historical durable job exit remains untouched, but the existing status path is overwritten and the copied snapshot is not fsynced.
findings.required_change: Use a recovery-specific status/output namespace. Read old source/status/receipts without writing them. If a separate current-status pointer is needed, label it as a new pointer and keep immutable predecessor paths.

findings.location: Admission at lines 260-284, EX install.lock, and pip command at line 791
findings.issue: The EX lock prevents overlapping invocations but there is no persistent one-attempt claim to reject a later invocation after failure/crash.
findings.evidence: After any failed new install, the old metadata-failure exit1 prerequisite is still true. The only replay short-circuit requires state=complete and valid TORCH_READY. A later invocation can enter pip again after a failed/unknown attempt.
findings.required_change: Create a unique recovery claim atomically with O_EXCL or open(x), fsync file and containing directory before the first mutation, bind source hash/frozen manifests/predecessor identity, and refuse all subsequent invocations when that claim exists, including failed or indeterminate states. Preserve it on cancellation.

findings.issue: The helper's ordinary-file wording and archive-validation scope are stronger than its actual checks.
findings.evidence: AST-extracted actual helper accepts FIFO and socket METADATA, duplicate payload members, and symlink payload members. It correctly rejects symlink METADATA, duplicate top-level METADATA, traversal, incorrect dist-info identity and duplicate Name headers.
findings.required_change: If strict ordinary-member/duplicate-payload validation is part of this recovery contract, reject duplicate archive names and non-regular non-directory member types (allow mode=0 ordinary ZIP entries). Otherwise describe this as top-level metadata identity validation, with whole-wheel frozen SHA validation as the remaining integrity boundary.
findings.limit: These controls do not show any malicious member in the frozen official wheel set; no security exploit or current data corruption is claimed.

findings.issue: The old waiter cannot be used as the Mamba successor after this recovery.
findings.evidence: STATUS_FOR_ROOT.md already acknowledges its old job/source binding. No new waiter or deployed successor identity was present in the reviewed local directory or fresh remote snapshot.
findings.required_change: Bind one separately controlled Mamba successor to the actual successful recovery receipt/source/job. Do not re-run the old waiter. Keep original wheel hashes and no automatic retries.

accepted_properties: Correctly selects only the sole top-level dist-info/METADATA while ignoring nested vendored distribution metadata.
Metadata identity helper is used both for verification and for proof before redundant-part cleanup.
Whole-wheel size/SHA checks, manifest SHA/pins, numeric-base version checks, EX install.lock and existing storage gates remain in the candidate.
The offline part path requires an existing complete part plus receipt and rejects identity mismatch; ordinary admission does not fall back to downloading.
No research code or 170-run budget changes are part of the inspected diff.

controls.execution_scope: Only AST-extracted metadata helper; no script top-level, network, pip, model or GPU execution.
